t: Learn what the Great One told your Draconid Friend.

Surface of the Astralophone flashes and you hear the familiar voice of your Draconid Friend:
Friend and brother! You my brother! The Father of Fire told so! You are brother to all! You helped!
What you want? You want I kill your relatives? You be free like fire! No debts! We often do so...
Oohh! The Father of Fire wants to tell me something! Wait!
One moment!

Surface of the Astralophone flashes again and you hear the whisper of your Draconid friend:
The Father of Fire has chosen the reward for you... He gave you this shard. He told it was important for you... Mine is happy, very happy!
Kill Astral Beater, Demon Bloodsucker and Bloody Malefic somewhere on the Twilight Isle. Report your success back to Draconids using Astralophone in the Overlord's Stronghold.

Surface of the Astralophone is shining brightly. You hear the voice of your Draconid Friend:
You are great warrior. Me knows! Me ask you. Demons kill.
One demon is small. But quick. It run and bite.
Another demon strong. Very-very strong! With big axe.
Third is sly. Third is shaman. Ouch!
Me ask you. Find three demons and kill. Find everywhere and kill. You are friend! You are strong! You help me.
Your Draconid Friend is waiting for your triumph. Don't let him down!

Draconid's voice is coming from the Astralophone full of joy:
You great warrior! You kill demons. You kill all three! Me so happy! We so happy! Chief also happy! Fire Father happy!
Now Chief speaks. Listen to Chief. Chief clever! Chief also your friend.
Bring Draconid Teeth Necklace to the Keeper of Knowledge in the Overlord's Stronghold.

A huge necklace made of teeth of different creatures proves your loyalty of Draconids. Such necklaces are usually worn by Draconid Leaders. You were the first one to receive such gift.
Keeper of Knowledge will be happy to have a look at it.
What a fancy necklace... Let me examine it.

Wonderful necklace! I can see teeth of various creatures in it: hydras, draconids... ahem... Humans, Elves and Orcs... This double tooth with a cavern belonged to a Troll! Unbelievable...
Draconids would not present such necklace to a stranger. It means that you are more than a friend to them. They trust you as if you were one of them. They are ready to fight on our side against Sarn!
Bring the mysterious Grimoir to Keeper of Knowledge at the Overlord's Citadel.

Strange book in leather cover is decorated with mysterious symbols. No one can tell what is written there as the language of the book is not known in any part of Sarnaut. There is not a single picture in it... You cannot decypher the Grimoir on your own.
Perhaps the Keeper of Knowledge will be glad to have a look at it.
Fascinating book! Is it a gift from our Wormface allies? Let me take a closer look.

I never had any doubts in you. I knew you would earn respect and trust of our allies! This book is written in ancient and now forgotten language. This language was used in the ages of the Junes. Even historians, the keepers of ancient knowledge, cannot understand what is written in this tome. But this language seems familiar to me.
I am absolutely sure that this book keeps the true history of the Wormfaces. This knowledge is priceless! I'll try to translate it, but it may take a lot of time.
It seems to me that reading the Grimoir is also a trial. The Wormfaces could have told us everything in our own language, as they normally do. They want you to translate the Grimoir because they want to make sure you are really interested in what they want to tell you.
Well, let's hope I finish the translation before we summon our allies to challenge Sarn. The most important thing is that you managed to win the trust of the Wormfaces!
Meet the Herald of Wrath in the docks near the Citadel.

You heart knows no mercy to Overlord's enemies. Time has come to encounter the enemy we both know well, but now you will play by our rules. I am speaking about cultists serving Overlord's worst enemy Sarn.
Don't you know the latest news? Sarn's servants, cultists and demons, decided to defy Overlord's power and attack the Citadel. Somewhere in deep Astral they managed to find another Yazes shard and turned it into their secret camp. Now after the overwhelming defeat at Gorluxor's Tower this shard is their last hope. They created a colossal astral ship out of the lifeless rock chunk splitted off from a solid Allod! Huge chains hanging from the Allod down into Astral serve as a harness for the most powerful demons living in Astral - octulhus. Their incredible power enables them to drag the isle across the Astral. And now it is rapidly approaching the Isle of Revelation.
Acolytes of Sarn not only intend to destroy the Citadel - they want to deprive the whole world of the opportunity to learn the Truth, destroying the Revelation!
They want war, and they will get it! We will attack first. Overloard's wrath will incinerate them! You and other Revelation seekers are about to become that wrath!
Set off to the east coast of the Isle of Revelation and meet the Herald of Wrath. He will lead the mission on intruding the cultist camp.
Go now and bring us a victory!
Did the Keeper of Knowledge send you?

Greetings! You are just on time. The ship is ready to sail to the Twilight Isle. Eternal twilight covers the cursed land and captured the hearts of those who decided to support Sarn.
You can help us to purify these lands. The light of truth will shine upon the ancient stones!

Make your way to the Twilight Isle coast on an Astral Sloop and talk to the Portal Keeper.
Use the Veil of Fog artifact to distract octulhus. If Demon Destroyers appear, use the Draconid Signal Horn to summon dragons. Astral Snipers can be easily destroyed using the Wave of Wrath artifact.

I am Overlord's Herald of Wrath! Overlord is merciful but his wrath knows no limit!
Sarn's minions, human cultists and demonic spawns, are going to destroy the Citadel. They gathered a strong army on their Twilight Isle, and demon guardians are whirling around it. We are going to strike them from the inside!
Our goal is to descent on the isle and regroup there. When we set up our defenses, we will open a portal for our army to destroy the enemy in its lair!
Operation Harpoon is aimed on penetrating the enemy's lair, and you are destined to be the pike of the harpoon.
A fast Astral sloop is waiting for the heroes at the dock. I will also give you a few artifacts to break through the demonic armada that defends the isle.
The first artifact is called Veil of Fog. Its power will avert gaze of the most dangerous demons, octulhus. As you come close to one of them, use the artifact, and the demons won't notice you.
The second artifact is the Draconid Signal Horn already familiar to you. If Demon Destroyers attack the sloop, blow the horn and our ally dragons will come to help.
Finally, the third artifact is called Wave of Wrath. During the whole way to the Twilight Isle your sloop will be attacked by lesser demons, Astral Snipers. Overlord's Wrath contained in the artifact will incinerate all of them!
Set off now and good luck to you, Seeker of Truth!
Remember that the sloop is designed only for one passenger! You will have to break through alone, there is only yourself to count on.
You did break through all the barriers! Unbelievable...
Overlord has sent me here to break into the hideout of Sarn's acolytes and kill them. I can open the Portal between this Isle and the Citadel, but only with your assistance.

Make your way to the Twilight Isle coast on an Astral Sloop and talk to the Portal Keeper.
Use the Veil of Fog artifact to distract octulhus. If Demon Destroyers appear, use the Draconid Signal Horn to summon dragons. Astral Snipers can be easily destroyed using the Wave of Wrath artifact.

Sarn's minions, human cultists and demonic spawns, are going to destroy the Citadel. They gathered a strong army on their Twilight Isle, and demon guardians are whirling around it. We are going to strike them from the inside!
Our goal is to descent on the isle and regroup there. When we set up our defenses, we will open a portal for our army to destroy the enemy in its lair!
Operation Harpoon is aimed on penetrating the enemy's lair, and you are destined to be the pike of the harpoon.
A fast Astral sloop is waiting for the heroes at the dock. I will also give you a few artifacts to break through the demonic armada that defends the isle.
The first artifact is called Veil of Fog. Its power will avert gaze of the most dangerous demons, octulhus. As you come close to one of them, use the artifact, and the demons won't notice you.
The second artifact is the Draconid Signal Horn already familiar to you. If Demon Destroyers attack the sloop, blow the horn and our ally dragons will come to help.
Finally, the third artifact is called Wave of Wrath. During the whole way to the Twilight Isle your sloop will be attacked by lesser demons, Astral Snipers. Overlord's Wrath contained in the artifact will incinerate all of them!
Set off now and good luck to you, Seeker of Truth!
Remember that the sloop is designed only for one passenger! You will have to break through alone, there is only yourself to count on.
You did break through all the barriers! Unbelievable...
Overlord has sent me here to break into the hideout of Sarn's acolytes and kill them. I can open the Portal between this Isle and the Citadel, but only with your assistance.
Gain access to the portals of Twilight Isle

We, Overlord's Scouts, managed to get to that cursed isle before there were too many demons around the coast. But I couldn't open the portal here! I did it a thousand times before, but the monster guarding the portal on the Isle is truly terrific! Apparently, it is filled with demonic foulness. I nearly jumped into the Astral with fear! Fortunately, we have found the way to restrain those fiends, and now the portal is at your service.
Hurry up, we have a little bit of time left!

I don't know how long I can keep the Portal open... The Guardian is in rage and is trying to close it. Perhaps I will need you help again later.
Now that the Portal is being kept open, allied troops of the Wormfaces and Draconids can start fighting the enemy. But we, as Overlord's vanguard, still have a lot to do...
Use acid and the hammer to smash 5 weak chain links. Report to the Headquarter Astralophone in Overlord's Stronghold. Pouring 3 vials of acid within 5 minutes destroys a chain link.

Huge pulsating scarlet letters are displayed on the Astralophone surface:
"Attention! Demons are trying to attack the Citadel. Troops stationed on the Twilight Isle must stop them at any cost.
To those who are faithful to their Overlord! Fight for your faith, for Sarnaut and the truth!"
The second part of the message is displayed below:
Chains hanging down from the edges of the isle serve as harness for powerful demons - octulhus. They are very strong and can drag the isle across the Astral! That's how they brought it to Misty Lands, and their next target is the Citadel! We must stop them!
All Seekers of Truth will receive hammers made of the strongest alloy, and a bottle of concentrated acid. The acid weakens chain links and makes them easier to destroy.
Hurry up! The cultists will try to fix the chains. The moment when they do that is depicted in your calendar. Come to the Astral Coast just before they arrive.
Destroy at least one of these chains. The cultists will need a lot of time to fix it."
Red letters are still burning on the surface of the Astralophone, warning you of the increased demonic activity.

Scarlet letters flash and another message appears:
"You made it! We saw how the chain collapsed and disappeared in the depths of the Astral. Cultists are no longer ready for a battle. They will spend all their resources to repair the chains.
Remember, Overlord encourages not only those who can bravely fight alone. If your guild helps us in the war against Sarn, if your comrades participate in upcoming battles against the Twilight Isle demons, the Prestige of your guild will increase incredibly."
Destroy as many demons and cultists on the Twilight Isle as possible. Report to the Headquarter Astralophone in Overlord's Stronghold.

Huge pulsating scarlet letters are displayed on the Astralophone surface:
"Attention! Demons are trying to attack the Citadel. Troops stationed on the Twilight Isle must stop them at any cost.
To those who are faithful to their Overlord! Fight for your faith, for Sarnaut and the truth!"
The second part of the message is displayed below:
Wait until the time specified in your calendar comes, and join the battle against the demons and their minions. All Seekers of Truth will fighting together against Overlord's foe!
Kill as many demons and cultists as possible! Let their rotten blood wash the rocks! No one dares to defy Overlord!
Let the pious fury fill your soul! Embrace the rage and act in the name of Overlord!"
Scarlet letters informing about the increased demon activity are still vivid on the surface of the Astralophone.

Scarlet letters flash and disappear, another message appears:
"Show no mercy to the enemies of the Overlord! Now you know that the cold fury of Truth can smash any obstacles, no matter whether it's just one demon or the whole army. After our victory, the cultists will not dare to attack the Citadel soon!
Remember, Overlord encourages not only those who can bravely fight alone. If your guild helps us in the war against Sarn, if your comrades participate in upcoming battles against the Twilight Isle demons, the Prestige of your guild will increase incredibly."
Scarlet letters informing about the increased demon activity are still vivid on the surface of the Astralophone.

Scarlet letters flash, and another message appears:
"Stay on course, Seeker of Truth! Demons suffer great losses, today they will not attempt to break into the Citadel. The enemy is not overthrown completely, and if tomorrow they attack again, we will hold another warm welcome."
Remember, Overlord encourages not only those who can bravely fight alone. If your guild helps us in the war against Sarn, if your comrades participate in upcoming battles against the Twilight Isle demons, the Prestige of your guild will increase incredibly."
Collect seven fragments of Zak's Crystal Armor scattered across the Misty Lands.

Before the battle against the June Curse, Ath-Zak, known as Zak to you, equipped his legendary armor made of diamonds - not just shiny gems sought by Sarnaut inhabitants, but high-purity diamond crystals that have souls of their own. These crystals also have a rare property - they greatly increase magic effects applied to their wearer. Protective spells of a Great Mage Tka-Rik, additionally enhanced by the crystals, allowed Zak to fight the Curse and destroy it.
However, the Curse managed to deliver the final blow to Zak, putting all its anger into it. No one would resist such power! Tka-Rik saved Zak, but the armor was broken and shattered into seven pieces. You need to collect the fragments of Zak's Crystal Armor.
I'm sure the enchantment cast on the armor will allow you to enter Tka-Rik Cave and learn the Revelation. Find the seven fragments, and I'll be able to restore the armor for you.
It won't be easy. Fragments were lost many years ago, and we only know the location of the first one. You will have to search for the rest by yourself.
If you bring me all seven fragments, I'll restore the Crystal Armor for you.
Congratulations! You have found all seven fragments. Let me complete the repair, and soon you'll be able to step into Tka-Rik's Cave, towards the Revelation!
Receive the Crystal Helmet from Overlord's Herald.

So, the Crystal Helmet. Yes, just a helmet so far. You'll receive the whole armor along with the Revelation. If you survive, of course.
This is exactly the same helmet that crowned Ath-Zak's head during his fight against the June Curse.
Tka-Rik, a Great Mage who died during the first demon invasion, sealed the cave with his postmortem will. Overlord additionally strengthened his magic using the greatest power in the world - the power of Zak's victory over June Curse.
Now only the one who wears this helmet will be able to get inside. Destructive veil protects the cave and the Revelation. Protects from demons, of course. I suppose you remember that the June Curse once had the appearance of a demon. One of the first demons in the world...
However, you'll learn the details from the Guardian of the Revelation. My job is to entrust you the Crystal Helmet.

It is rightfully yours.
Helmet of Knowledge. Helmet of Wisdom. Helmet of the Revelation...
Wait a minute! I haven't finished yet! Once they hear that word, they rush to the Revelation...
Listen to me first, I have something to say.
Go through the destructive veil that protects Tka-Rik's Cave and meet the Guardian of the Revelation.

So. Here it is - the most important task in your life!
Go through the Destructive Veil that protects Tka-Rik's Cave and meet the Guardian of the Revelation. Find out the truth about this world.
May Overlord protect you!

You are here...
It means you are allowed to know the truth about this world. I'm here to help you.
Whisper in your head says: "The experiment must go on... Don't stop, no matter what's happening."

When you touch the cold surface of Astralophone, you can hear a hissing voice of a Wormface:
"So, the first phase of the experiment is complete. The results are not yet clear, but we don't have enough time for detailed analysis. It's time to start the second phase."
Confirm that you are ready to keep the secret of the Wormfaces.

Instead of text, the Astralophone surface is lit with bright glow. You hear rustling voice of a Wormface:
"Overmind welcomes you, friend. We need your help in an important experiment.
But before we get your consent, we want you to know that we value the ability to keep silence higher than diligence. No one should know what we plan and what instructions you receive from us.
Are you willing to keep our secret?"

Even such an unusual way of communication can't hide notes of relief that are heard in Wormface's voice:
"We trust you.
Not because we have no other options, but because we are tired of distrust. Sometimes a moment comes when one should forget about the past and make a step into the future."
Confirm that you are ready to keep the secret of the Wormfaces.

Instead of text, the Astralophone surface is lit with bright glow. You hear rustling voice of a Wormface:
"Overmind welcomes you, friend. We need your help in an important experiment.
But before we get your consent, we want you to know that we value the ability to keep silence higher than diligence. No one should know what we plan and what instructions you receive from us.
Are you willing to keep our secret?"

Even such an unusual way of communication can't hide notes of relief that are heard in Wormface's voice:
"We trust you.
Not because we have no other options, but because we are tired of distrust. Sometimes a moment comes when one should forget about the past and make a step into the future."
Use the mysterious device on Flesh Torturer and kill him. Report to the Astralophone in Overlord's Stronghold.

Wormface is whispering over the Astralophone:
"Here comes the second phase of the experiment. Demons Weepers are not strong enough to destroy... er... well, the first phase proved that they didn't fit. This is why one of the most powerful demons, known as Flesh Torturer, is required for the second phase. We hope that the strength absorbed by the artifact will provide the effect we need. Haven't you thought that this artifact absorbs the power of killed demons? Are you incapable of scientific analysis at all?! We can't tell you so far what it is for. Just trust us, we are your friends.
You will find Flesh Torturer to the far southeast of the Overlord's Stronghold, at the Astral Coast. Activate the device and destroy the demon. You will do a great favor for us and for the whole world by killing that dangerous beast. Don't be surprised if you notice something strange to the device. Everything is under control."

Notes of impatience are heard in the voice of the Wormface on the Twilight Isle: "Have you killed the Flesh Torturer? No? What are you waiting for? Experiment must be completed as soon as possible! We count on you."

Genuine rejoice is heard in Wormface's voice through the noise. Surely he's pleased with your progress:
"Great! The device worked perfectly! The second phase of experiment went in full accordance with our expectations. There is one last step, and it will be completed."
Use the mysterious device on Bumpy and defeat the demon.

The voice of the Wormface is shivering with impatience:
"Overmind is satisfied, my friend. Your assistance is truly invaluable. If our scientists made no mistakes in their calculations, we need to kill one more demon to complete the experiment.
This demon is incredibly strong, but we are sure you can defeat him. Even more powerful enemies died by your hand!
Bumpy has been frequently seen at the foothill of the Gloomy Rocks. Don't forget to activate the device before the battle. Go now! We'll be waiting for the result."
Wow! The device is destroyed... Was it supposed by the experiment?

Strange Spark is hovering above the ground.
It appeared as soon as a mysterious device of the Wormfaces exploded... Was it hidden inside all this time? But whose Spark it is?
Deliver the Strange Spark to the top of the Dragon Peak and meet the one who is awaiting you.

The Spark is shining with a dim light. It grows and becomes brighter, and eventually you see nothing but the light all around...
You see a vision.
A narrow path curls through the mountains. It seems this place is somewhere in the Gloomy Rocks to the north from here. A vague figure is walking down the road with an opalescent Spark hovering nearby. This figure seems to be... you!
The demons are attacking the figure and the Spark. They are dying, one by one.
The Spark and you are reaching the top of the rock, wing clapping can be heard, and something enormous is descending from above, powerful and dangerous. There is no choice... This is the creature you must challenge.
The vision disappears, you see the Spark slowly hovering upwards and landing into your hands. It seems the Spark wants you to find this place in the Gloomy Rocks. Was it a part of the Wormfaces's plan?

Mortal!
Have you brought what we need?

Hmm... Have we met before?
I don't think so. I hate your kind. I mean people, elves, gibberlings, orcs... All of you. If I meet someone, it usually ends with their death!
There may be exceptions, anyway... For example, you.
I'm executing the will of a more powerful creature than you can imagine. It is the only reason I'm talking to you and... urrrgh!... I should even reward you, as required by the agreement...
Confirm that you understand what Agrus told you.

I'm taking this Spark away from you. All this mess was started because of it...
Don't even ask me whose Spark it was! I want to forget it... You think that I, the Great Dragon, would have helped to resurrect one of... one of those who killed my brethren?
But this is a part of a deal between my kin and the Wormfaces. We are granting them this life, and they will return us another one...
Enough of it! No living or dead soul should know about the Spark and our conversation! If you leak a word you will die! Do you understand?
Do you want to stay alive, mortal?

Good decision.
I've got what you were searching for... A fragment of Crystal Armor. I should give it to you. This is a payment for your silence. It is much safer when a person keeps silence not only because of their fear...
With this fragment you will soon find the truth... But I don't think you will like it, mortal.
Farewell! If everything goes as intended, we'll never see each other again. Don't expect me to miss you! Ha ha...

Make use of the Will Suppressor and capture the body of a cultist. Find the secret documents in Desecrated City and hide them among the stones near the Overlord's Stronghold. Then break the mental link with the cultist, get the documents from the cache and deliver them to the Will Suppressor.

Signal lamp flashes over Will Suppressor, and a low imperious voice sounds from the speaker:
"Seeker of Truth! Are you already familiar with this device, a creation of Overmind and Overlord's Servants? No? Then listen to me carefully.
You can use this device to control the mind of another creature for a short time and manipulate its body like your own. In the meanwhile your own body will be lying peacefully in the sarcophagus inside the Will Suppressor. The device has undergone field tests successfully. We are entrusting you the honor to carry out the final test.
The task is simple. While you are lying in the sarcophagus, your mind should seize the body of a cultist. As soon as you establish control, make a small sabotage. Take cultist documents out of the chest hidden in the depths of Desecrated City, and put them into the stones to the east of the Stronghold. If everything goes smoothly, the cultist won't remember anything. You will only have to take the documents out of the cache and pass the information to us.
Keep in mind: we want a clear experiment. You have to pass this test alone. Don't try asking your friends to help you, or you will fail."
You should hurry up and deliver the documents...

The voice coming out of the speaker is full of discontent:
"This... this is not what we were looking for at all! The papers are worthless... Well, a negative result is still a result. Let's have another try tomorrow. Thank you."
Bring the fragment to Overlord's Herald in the Citadel.

The fragment is glistening and sparkling with warm glare coming out of the cold stone. Mighty ancient magic is concealed in that lifeless crystal, and if someone manages to set it free, the barrier blocking the entrance to Tka-Rik's Cave will fall.
Give the fragment to Overlord's Herald. He will keep it until you collect the remaining pieces.

Another piece of armor that belonged to the ancient June hero. Wonderful!
I will take it from you and keep it until all the fragments are found.

Mortals can't keep a treasure that falls into their hands. Yes, I found the fragment you've lost. Take it back if you want.
But if you bother me again, I'll bite your head off!
Bring the fragment to Overlord's Herald in the Citadel.

The fragment is glistening and sparkling with warm glare coming out of the cold stone. Mighty ancient magic is concealed in that lifeless crystal, and if someone manages to set it free, the barrier blocking the entrance to Tka-Rik's Cave will fall.
Give the fragment to Overlord's Herald. He will keep it until you collect the remaining pieces.

Another piece of armor that belonged to the ancient June hero. Wonderful!
I will take it from you and keep it until all the fragments are found.

Let me ask you for a favor. When you return to Nezebgrad, find Yasker, the most influential and dangerous man in the Empire, and whisper the following words into his ear: "I'm the one who knows the Truth. Isn't it time for you to set off to the Isle of Revelation?"
Don't be afraid. You have done so many great deeds, I'm sure this little joke will pass unpunished.

Stop! Don't say a word.
I know everything. You were in Tka-Rik's Cave and now you know the truth.
You can be proud. You were there in person! Back in Nezeb's times, best minds of the Empire puzzled their brains over the secrets of the past. They were analyzing the events, discussing different theories. No one in their worst dream could even imagine that our world is a prison created by one god for another!
One thing I understand clearly: in the nearest future we are going to make a choice - either we obey our creator and help him to set free, or we betray him for the sake of our happy lives.
Junes made the choice in their times. And where are they now? Who they turned into? Do you want to follow their way? Would it be right?
Think about that.
And think about another thing: what made Wormfaces and dragons defy the gods? What did they hope for? What do they know that we don't?

Let me ask you for a favor. When you return to Novobgrad, find Aidenus, the most influential and dangerous man in the League, and whisper the following words into his ear: "I'm the one who knows the Truth. Isn't it time for you to set off to the Isle of Revelation?"
Don't be afraid. You have done so many great deeds, I'm sure this little joke will pass unpunished.

You too...
You are not the one who reminds me of the fact that our world has changed...
I'm not going anywhere - I'm old and I've seen enough to believe your words. You are not the first one to come running here, believing you are a great messiah who just learned the Truth.
If I say I knew everything beforehand, it would be a lie. I didn't.
I've been guessing, making up elaborate theories, arguing with my teachers and students, thinking it over and over again.
And you just got everything on a platter. You know the truth about our world. This is a prison for a god suffering from schizophrenia. Or a theater stage for a barnstormer in need of audience?
What are you going to do with this knowledge? Huh? Have you thought about that?
I have. Here is my revelation to you. In the nearest future we will have to make the most difficult choice. Not between right and wrong - it would be easy. The choice between one wrong and another. As Junes did once. Were they mistaken? What would you do if you were them? Or... what will you do being yourself?
Think.
There is one hope for me in this story. The determination of the Great Dragons and the Wormfaces to defy Nihaz. It means there is something that gives them ground to believe in their victory. I wish I knew what it is.
Find the cultist message and bring it to Wise Pathfinder in Overlord's Stronghold.

I received a word from the Citadel. It concerns both you and our enemies, servants of the demonic cult.
Scouts on the Revelation Isle reported a big well-trained group of cultists fighting their way to the Tka-Rik's Cave entrance. Cultists managed to neutralize the defensive spell surrounding the cave for a short time, so they got inside. Our scouts couldn't follow them. They heard the sounds of combat from the depth of the cave. After a while, a single fighter came out. He was wounded, worn out by a mighty spell. Life was leaving him quickly. The only thing our scouts could learn was that he was covering his captain till the last minute. The captain fled back to the Twilight Isle with a message.
Any information concerning Tka-Rik's Cave is vitally important for us. Start searching among cultists, perhaps this message contains something that might help us see into their motives.
How is your search going, Truth Seeker?

Aha! I had no doubt that someone managed to escape and deliver the message.
Let's see what you have got...
Find the other part of the Blood-Stained Scroll and bring both parts to Wise Pathfinder in Overlord's Stronghold.

The scroll is torn and smeared with blood. Lower part of it is missing. Unfortunately, a part of the text is illegible, but the remained fragment contains information that can be useful.
This scroll is a cultists' report of an attempt to break into Tka-Rik's Cave. "Ancient Guard", "Magic of the Ancients" and "Deadly Glow" are mentioned in the scroll several times.
You should try and find the second part of the scroll. Keep an eye on Cultist Defilers...
If you find both parts, it will be more clear what the cultists were searching in the cave and what stopped them.

Interesting... So, the cultists managed to break through the magic barrier and enter the cave. They met an Ancient Guardian there who killed most of them with a deadly magic, "the spell of the Ancient Ones" - that is how the cultists refer to Junes.
So this Ancient Guard is a June creation... But I have never heard that golems, the only June creations that survived to this day, were capable of using magic. I suspect that you will meet something unknown in Tka-Rik's Cave.
Bring the message about Tka-Rik's Cave to Wise Pathfinder in Overlord's Stronghold.

Small holes along the edge of the scroll indicate that it was stapled to another paper. There must have been additional orders attached!
Continue your searches! I'm sure that cultists had more papers, they can lead us to understanding of what will happen to you in Tka-Rik's Cave.
Keep an eye on Cultist Assassins. They are the elite troops of cultists' army, eyes and ears of Hierarchs. I have no doubt they are aware of the expedition to Tka-Rik's Cave.

Oh! Very interesting...
The message is encrypted, but the cipher is so primitive that it's easy to understand what it is about.
Kill Lawrence Weirdin, take the Fragment of Crystal Armor from him and bring it to Overlord's Herald in the Citadel.

One of the papers you found contains an order of a Cultist Hierarch. He commands his most loyal servants, Cultist Assassins, to make every effort and find the fragments of Zak's Crystal Armor! It seems they are unaware that you've already found most of the fragments.
Cultists managed to find one fragment. It's kept at Lawrence Weirdin, runaway Xadaganian explorer who participated in research of June heritage under the Committee's order.
I don't know how cultists make people like Weirdin cooperate. But then again, even the Great Mage Gorluxor fell for Sarn's persuasion and headed the Cult.
In any case, you have to take the fragment away from Weirdin, and certainly he won't give it without a fight.

Wow! Even a legion of demons couldn't stop you!
Not only you tricked cultists, but received another fragment! It's time for the Cult to give up the idea to break into the cave. Only the one who restored the armor of the greatest June hero deserves to learn the Revelation!
I'll keep this fragment and preserve it until the time is right.

Message on the surface of Astralophone says:
"Astral Hounds inhabiting the Twilight Isle found an opportunity to assault the Draconid Isle and destroy their eggs. If they continue their raids, Draconids won't help us in the upcoming battle. All their forces will be aimed at saving their children.
We can't leave our allies without support. You are entrusted with a task of killing as many Astral Hounds as possible. The Draconids will be very grateful, you'll see."
The surface of Astralophone remains cold and lifeless. You might have not completed the task yet...

Fancy letters appears on the surface of Astralophone:
"Elimination of Hounds is confirmed. Congratulations!
But don't be satisfied with what you have achieved already. Every enemy you kill brings us closer to victory!"

Letters appear on the cold surface of the Astralophone:
"Rumors coming from larger Allods say that cultists recruit more followers into their ranks. Demonic Cult Servants are everywhere, bringing discord to Sarnaut inhabitants. Here, on Twilight Isle, they are preparing their adepts to go out to the big world and bring neophytes to the Cult.
All Seekers of Truth on Twilight Isle are entrusted with an assignment to kill as many Demonic Cult Servants as possible."
Astralophone surface remains dark and lifeless.

A new message appears on the surface of Astralophone:
"Elimination of Servants of the Demonic Cult is confirmed. Well done!
Let all Overlord's enemies meet this fate!"
Participate in killing Ash, the leader of Astral Hounds and report to Headquarter Astralophone in Overlord's Stronghold.

Scarlet symbols flash on the surface of the Astralophone:
"Our observers watching the Twilight Isle coast noticed a surprisingly large and angry male Astral Hound whose hide is night black. Other Hounds cringe before him. We called that demon Ash.
All heroes on the Twilight Isle are assigned to kill Ash. The demon can be found in the southern part of the Isle, on the border of the Desecrated City and Astral Coast."
Astralophone surface is dark. You have no new messages.

Fancy fiery letters appear on the surface of the Astralophone:
"The death of Ash must have disturbed the pack of Astral Hounds. They won't be so dangerous anymore and will never show their noses outside of the Isle until a new leader emerges."
Surface of the Astralophone is blank and cold. There are no new messages.

Flaming letters are displayed on the surface of the Astralophone:
"Great! We have received the trophies and started the research. Hopefully we will manage to disclose the secret of the new alloy. If we need more weapon to analyze, we'll inform you. Thanks for the excellent job!"

A new message appears on the surface of the Astralophone:
"Good job! First results are already obtained. Unfortunately, we couldn't disclose the connection between demons and cultists yet. Cultist heart is no different from a heart of an ordinary Sarnaut's habitant.
Perhaps they just lack material for experiments? If they need new specimens for research we'll inform you."
Bring Aristarkh Zlobin' Diary to the Headquarter Astralophone.

Luminous letters appear on the cold surface of the Astralophone:
"Have you heard of Aristarkh Zlobin? No? Well, isn't it a proof that the glory is not eternal...
He was once one of the most experienced and skilled commanders of the Imperial Army. He became famous for his determination and ability to plan very complex missions. No one could have imagined that Zlobin would defect to our enemies and serve to the Demonic Cultists and Sarn.
What did break his will? If we manage to find out how the cultists recruit new adherents, we will use this knowledge to our benefit.
It is known that Zlobin kept a diary where he noted everything that happened to him and his squad. All his thoughts, feelings and actions... There must be a record of the event that pushed him to the enemy's side!
Find Zlobin at the Astral Coast of the Twilight Isle, kill him and bring his diary to the Headquarter Astralophone."
A warning appears on the surface of the Astralophone: "You must find Aristarkh Zlobin's Diary. Don't waste your time."

The message on the Astralophone surface says:
"Don't be surprised that the diary looks like an issue of "Pointy Ears" magazine. Its pages are most certainly covered by some code. We couldn't decipher it yet, but we won't abandon our attempts. Many of the Citadel inhabitants are interested in this research, too. Thanks for your excellent job."
Get on board of the Astral Sloop and go to the Twilight Isle.

Our landing is not going as smooth as we'd like to... Demons are attacking our ships, cultists give no mercy to fighters trying to open a portal to Overlord's Stronghold.
You weren't lucky today, too, were you? Many heroes perished in battle. Some of them didn't have your luck, and their Sparks disintegrated in the endless Astral...
But despite to the losses, we must keep assaulting the Twilight Isle. If you are ready, Astral Sloop is waiting for you.
Remember that you can only travel there alone! If you are in a party or a raid, the way will be closed.
May the Overlord's powers keep you safe!
Our enemy is strong, but we are not giving ground!
You are just in time. The Isle is swarming with demons and cultists. Any help will be useful!
Go to Draconid Island to find out what happened to the Demon Hunter expedition.

You remember Alexey Borodin, don't you? The hunter emissary who helped you befriend the draconids? Well, it looks like he and his friends are in trouble.
Before that despicable betrayal took place he and I used to correspond virtually every day. He would send me letters with one of his subordinates. Thanks to his reports we have learned a lot about the draconids' culture and religion.
But now I've lost all contact with him! No one has returned from the island yet. The Keeper of Power has sent his scouts there, but they too have disappeared without a trace.
Please, should your journey take you to Draconid Island, find out what happened to the Demon Hunters. They are a fine bunch, and I really don't want to believe that they are dead...
Go talk to the Master's Voice to get to Draconid Island. It knows what should be done.

The body is so disfigured that you cannot even recognize the face! Poor bastard...
But at least now you know what happened to the expedition: everyone was massacred by draconids. Or perhaps someone managed to survive?
Find Alexey Borodin on Draconid Island.

Looks like the camp was attacked suddenly. The hunters had scarcely realized what was going on before they were literally torn to shreds! There's blood and signs of struggle everywhere...
Indeed, though they were taken by surprise, the demon hunters sold their lives dearly! They died like heroes.
And yet, oddly enough Alexey Borodin is not among the disfigured bodies! Could it be that the battle-hardened veteran has managed to survive and is hiding somewhere on the island?
This must be verified!

Cough... Did they really send someone to our aid?
Too late... Dead! They're dead, you hear me?! All my friends are dead! Killed by those goddamn draconids! We were attacked at night while we were asleep! Can you imagine? A horde of toothy beasts bursts from the darkness, shouting some crap about the Master's betrayal and death to all his servants... They simply overwhelmed us.
I'm the only one who managed to draw a weapon and slay a couple of those bastards. Then I was forced back and down to the shore, where I sustained a few wounds. I had no option but to flee. What a disgrace...
I should have stayed with them... With my hunter friends... Till the last drop of blood... I was right to never have trusted those beasts!
You will help me exact vengeance, won't you?
Place the heads of Ghash and Urgash on the altar and return to Alexey Borodin.

Vengeance! That is what I seek!
My companions' deaths must be avenged. Those scaly beasts must cower and flee when they hear someone mention the demon hunters. Or maybe we should call ourselves draconid hunters, eh?
I know how to sow horror in the hearts of those loathsome traitors. The kind of horror they've never experienced. But since I'm wounded, you shall be the instrument of my vengeance!
I saw an altar here on the island where the draconids offer sacrifices to their deity. They call this thing "Fiery Father." Ha! We'll see how it will like the heads of its own offspring put on the altar!
Ghash, the drake chieftain, and Urgash, the draconid leader... Their heads on the altar shall be stuff of nightmares for those who killed my friends!
I won't find peace until my comrades are avenged!

Yes! Those filthy beasts shall remember this day and this hour for a long time! They shall curse the moment they had decided to commit their perfidious attack.
Thank you from the bottom of my heart, comrade!
The souls of my fallen comrades long for revenge. What can be more frightening than true death?

I heard the desperate screams and dying wheezing of the winged beasts. Well done, comrade.
The drakes shall remember this day as one of just retribution. And that's what all traitors should expect!
Kill Ghash, the drake chieftain, and bring his head to Alexey Borodin.

Remember Ghash, the drake chieftain? The one you were sparring with?
It's time to prove you're equally proficient in real combat. Remember where to find him? Well, I'll remind you. Ghash dwells in the mountains to the east of here.
Destroy him! With their chieftain dead, the drakes will start to quarrel, and we'll add some fuel to the fire. I have an idea... Chop his head off and bring it to me. I'll find a suitable application for that brainless skull.
We should have exterminated all those beasts while we were at the Dragon Ring...

Yes! His dying roar made even cliffs shake. And the surviving drakes were darting around the sky like headless chickens.
It was an unforgettable sight!
Kill 3 mature draconid sorcerers and 3 wise draconid healers and return to Alexey Borodin.

I don't know exactly who took part in the raid on our camp. All draconids look the same to me. But that doesn't mean we'll refrain from revenge!
Go to their village and kill as many draconids as you can. If we can't take revenge on the actual killers, we'll take revenge on their entire race. Blood for blood, death for death! I'm not interested in regular warriors, they're just an instrument. It's those damn priests and sorcerers that I want! They've turned the draconids against us. Them and their terrible god...
Please destroy them! Help me exact vengeance!
If anyone is to be punished, it's the strongest and most experienced draconids. If the elimination of our squad was planned, it is those bastards who are the culprits.
Oh... My wounds are getting worse. But I won't die until my friends are avenged!
I can see their cold blood on your hands... No need to say anything. My comrades would have been grateful.
Kill Urgash, the draconid chieftain, and bring his head to Alexey Borodin.

Urgash, that goddamn hypocrite bastard! He smiled, assuring me of our eternal friendship, called me friend and brother... But once I turned my back, he shoved his blade into it!
Herein lies a sorrowful lesson... You can trust no one! We were wrong about the draconids' loyalty. That misconception cost my comrades-in-arms their lives.
An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth. Urgash must die! That traitor deserves no mercy.
Unfortunately, my wounds won't let me revel in his last breath. Therefore, bring me his head! I want to look into his glazed-over eyes!
I look forward to my wounds healing, so that I can wield a blade to avenge my fallen friends.

Is Urgash dead? Praised be the gods! I fear to imagine how much grief that (literally!) cold-blooded traitor could have brought to our kind.
His head will make a perfect decoration for the draconids' altar. Let them tremble, for the hand of retribution shall strike them all!
Bring 5 drake claws and 5 draconid fangs to Slark-Slark at the dockside of Draconid Island.

Halt! We don't wish to fight. We wish to speak.
You used to help our enemies. Now you're fighting them. The enemy of our enemy can be our friend. If you help us, we are willing to forgive you.
But first you have to prove you truly are an enemy to the draconids. Bring me five drake claws and five draconid fangs. Then we'll be able to trust you.
The draconids' deaths bring me joy. That'll teach them how to steal our eggs!

Five fangs and five claws... Excellent!
Now we believe that you are, like us, a true enemy of the draconids. We're ready to forgive you for your past misdeeds.

Listen to what I've got to say.
You can make amends for the evil your race has done to ours. And bring plenty of sorrow to those blasted draconids along the way.
I'm talking about the eggs. Those stolen from our village. Get them back! We want our kids back! As for the draconids, let them all die out without any offspring.
And remember: grab only those eggs that are still ours. Those that now belong to the draconids should be broken, if possible.
That's it. Now go. We'll be waiting for you.
Eggs... Our eggs... Our offspring... Oh, how I've missed them.

Stranger, I can't believe my eyes. You've made it!
Now the draconids may fly off the handle because they won't be able to steal our kids again.
Thank you, stranger. Please accept this reward as a token of my gratitude for what you've done.
Go to Draconid Island and locate saboteur Roman Lazeykin.

I hope you've got no pressing matters to attend to? I've been waiting too long for someone I can entrust this important mission to. Listen carefully, as there's very little time left.
The treacherous draconids have gone ahead to a small allod we call the Frontier. Some of the draconids remained on the Island, however, posing a serious threat to the Citadel.
I've sent a couple of scouts there, those who are obedient to the Master's Will. Plenty of time has passed and I still haven't heard from them.
Please go to Draconid Island and find Roman Lazeykin. Find out what he was able to learn, and then proceed as you see fit. We must eliminate the threat posed by the draconids as soon as possible!
When you're ready, go talk to the Master's Voice. It will help you teleport to the Island.
Freeze! Move and I'll shoot you dead! Who are you? Answer quickly!

So that's how it is... Those pompous Sentinels finally remembered that we exist!
You want to know where my partner is? Caught by the draconids, that's where! Now they're rotting away in a cage.
Why "they"? Because my partners are gibberlings! The Rowdy Family! Rowdy they are, no doubt... When the draconids attacked us, they charged right into the scuffle. Got captured and thrown into a guarded cage. Now what can I do, all alone? I don't even know how to help them. I feel sorry for them - they're like little kids who don't know any better.
Look, help me, will you? You know about the rule in the Imperial army, "Help a comrade in need, even if it means your end"!
So here's the situation: the cage is to the east, and there's only one guard who keeps the key on him all the time. No one else. Whack the guard, free those silly fuzzies and bolt!
Hey, we're here! Let us out!
Oh...Thanks a lot! We thought we were goners for sure, soon to be devoured by that scaly filth!
Escort the Rowdy Family and Roman Lazeykin to the docks on Draconid Island.

We fought like lions! Bam - one down! Crushed another! Grabbed the third by the tail and tossed him! The fourth lost a few teeth! The fifth... We smacked him as high as we could reach. Serves him right!
Then we were captured... Jeez... They threatened to eat us! Only they couldn't agree on how - boil, fry, or gut and roast over fire. Awful, just awful! Next time we won't be so easy on the bastards! And we'll be that much smarter about it, too!
Anyway, enough chit-chat. They can spot us and throw us right back into the next empty cage.
Let's get back to Lazeykin. He might be an imperial subject, but he's a good friend who didn't leave us when we needed him!

Rowdies! My darlings! Alive and kicking!
Gosh... I thought I'd never see you again!
Thank you, friend, for helping out!
Locate a clutch of draconid eggs and find a way to destroy them. Then return to Roman Lazeykin at the dockside of Draconid Island.

Now that the Rowdies are safe, it's time to get to what we've come here for - sabotage!
Listen up. As you remember, there are clutches of draconid eggs here on the island. Something you are partially responsible for, incidentally. Which means you'll also be the one to correct this mistake.
Locate a clutch and find a way to break the eggs. If we succeed, the draconids will have no future. Without new fighters, their defeat in the war will be a matter of time.
Regretfully, neither the Rowdies nor I can assist you on this mission. We've been seriously beaten up in that scuffle. I'll send the Rowdies to the Citadel so that the little ones get some rest, which they badly deserve. I myself will stay here to wait for news from you.
Now go, and don't delay. We have lots and lots to do.
I hope you've got some good news?

Acid, you say... Yes, that's possible. Besides, I think it's the only option.
But that doesn't mean I like it! Then again, what can you do? A mission is a mission.
This egg is broken! I wonder how that happened?
Soften the shells of 5 draconid eggs with acid, break the eggs and report to the Keeper of Power at the Master's Citadel.

That's what they call peace, heh... No, old grudges cannot be forgotten in a matter months. No way they can... A single spark was enough for the flame of animosity to flare up anew.
But perhaps we can take advantage of it. While the wormfaces are fighting the draconids, we'll take them out one at a time. Anyway, that's not for us to worry about. We have our mission.
The clutch needs to be destroyed. Luckily, and in no small part thanks to you and our former wormfaced friends, I now know what needs to be done. If they use acid to destroy draconid egg shells, then we can do the same. You get the idea?
I have a few acid bottles that I had planned to use for a different purpose, but now... It's better to make use of them here.
So grab the bottles and go! Splash some acid on an egg and hit it with all your might. Break five eggs and then we'll see what those scaly beasts will do when left without their offspring! And we'll be there to direct their rage on the wormfaces. Now that's what I call two birds with one stone!
What news do you bring, Keeper of the Revelation?

Great news! You've rid us of a heavy burden. Now that the draconid threat is eliminated, the Citadel inhabitants will breathe easier.
I'm grateful beyond words. Yet I hope you'll find my gift to your liking.

Look, with you here and some of the draconids off somewhere in the Misty Lands, we need to take advantage of the situation. What do you say?
Not many draconids stayed here on the island, but they are still a threat to flank us. It would be wise to get rid of that threat.
So let's not waste any time! Go kill as many draconids as you can. The only thing I can say after their betrayal is this: the only good draconid is a dead draconid!
Heh, I'd be glad to get some exercise, but I'm here to gather information. I mustn't die in battle.
Meet chieftain Smack the Lakefolk at Eldress Lake.

Listen up, soldier! We need to talk.
Here's the deal. Drabova says you're planning to fight a golem? Heh, and they say we orcs are stupid and always trying to solving our problems with brute force... They say we have to use our heads, hah!
Well, now we're at peace with those slimies. They've been living in their puddle for who knows how many decades, and they've seen our wormfaced friends rest... resto... I mean, fix that massive golem!
And if I were you, I'd talk to the slimies' leader before trying to climb the bayonets ass first. Perhaps you'll work out a better idea, eh!

Howdy, beanpole! Come on in, make yourself at home. The lakefolk are always glad to see you!
Are you here on business or just dropping by for some fish soup?

How terribly clumsy! You adventurers can't be trusted with anything! Adventure is all you think about!
But this is your lucky day, for I have found your mask. Here, take it and don't lose it again!

Among all caves on Frontier, I would suspect the one that is being so persistently obstructed by the brave Watchful family. And since the Wormfaces are equally persistent in their attempts to clear it, I am pretty sure that the temple you are looking for is located there.
h: Ask if there is a cave that matches the description

t: Let me think. Destroyers only dwell on this allod, which means their temple must be somewhere on Frontier. We haven't seen anything looking like a temple, which means it is hidden somehow. Most likely, under the ground. How do we get under the ground? Through a cave, obviously!
h: Tell about the Destroyers and the key

t:
I take it you're afraid of the big rattler? Well, you should be! We didn't used to fear it. What's there to fear? A block of stone lying at the bottom of the lake, covered in slit with only its head sticking out?
But then one night I heard a rattle! I went to check it out and saw a swarm of tiny little rattlers. They were all over, making all kinds of noise, toppling the fences and scaring away the fish... I almost had a heart attack! But they didn't react at all. They lined up around the lake and just stood there, waiting. And then one of them stepped forward, holding this strange this, all glowing and iridescent. He pointed it at the lake, and the water erupted with waves, one bigger than the other! Three of my nets were washed away... Brand new ones, too - a real pity! Anyway, I looked at the lake and saw this mass rising up from the center of the lake - a big rattler! I literally froze in fear. Perhaps it had been asleep, not dead, and the small rattler woke him up with that thing before falling asleep himself. The big rattler grabbed the small one and dragged him away. The other rattlers followed suit, leaving the strange thing behind. I picked it up once fear released me. I sensed something about this thing, that it was important... But I won't just give it to you.
Let's trade! I'll give you the thing and you help me out with a small affair. See all those drakes on the cliffs? They've been picking on us, stealing our fish, ruining the nets and setting our houses on fire... I'm so sick of them!
So let's do this: you take care of the drakes for us and I'll give you this thing, whatever it is, OK? You'll find good use for it, I swear by the toad!
Oh! You're our best friend of all! In our village you'll always find food and shelter. Only you won't find that thing... That thing has been stolen!
Find the crab that stole the "strange thing" in Eldress Lake and take it back. Then bring the June artifact to Semer Shabas at the Outpost.

We don't have the strange thing... I took it with me when I left the house, sat down on the shore and started fixing the net. I put the thing next to me to keep an eye on it. I got distracted with all the knots, and when I looked up I saw a crab crawling by. There's lots of them in the lake, massive ones too. I got all happy, thinking dinner was coming my way. I bent down to grab the harpoon, and that's when I saw the thing in its pincers! I forgot all about the harpoon and started chasing the crab, but... It reached the water in a matter of seconds... I feel terrible, but there's no way I can help you now. We're small and those crabs are huge. I can't defeat the beast in the water. But you're a beanpole, I'm sure you can handle it. Only I don't know which of them got the thing. Hmm...
Why are you distracting me? Can't you see I'm busy?!
Wait a sec... That's the June golem control mechanism! What a find... Where did you manage to get it?
Get 75 power cells by fighting golems at the Frontier and return to Semer Shabas.

How curious... So, you're saying this artifact helped regular golems raise the huge Guardian from the bottom of the lake? Well, that explains a number of things!
This thing must be a remote control. The ancient Junes were quite militaristic at the dawn of their civilization. They hid war machines in a bunch of secret places to use should the need arise. It appears that the guardian watching the portal is one such reserve machine.
Back then the Junes integrated separate power cells into their golems. After all, the crystals that power golems could be destroyed, while a golem with a built-in power supply could operate without recharging for a long time. When the wormfaces came here, they discovered one of the old hiding places, switched on the old golems and then the Guardian.
As for the artifact you've found, things aren't as simple. As far as I understand, it's broken and quite useless for us at this point. Perhaps it was ruined by water or some internal component is out of order. Could be I'll be able to fix and even modify it to work as a key to the portal and a friendly-or-hostile detector so that the Guardian doesn't attack you. But for that I'll need golem power cells. And lots of them! We'll have to disassemble at least seventy golems to understand their design and fix your "remote".

A very interesting artifact... Perhaps we've actually surpassed the Junes in several fields of technology and magic. That said, we've still got ways to go to compete with them in integrating magical and physical devices into operational mechanisms!

Everything's ready! I removed the unnecessary parts, made a few adjustments and charged it with energy. Now this thing is your ticket out of here. With this device you can easily get to the old portal without disturbing the guardian. Were I you, however, I'd kill him anyway, since it poses a serious threat to all of us. Besides, I'm also curious what he's got on the inside!

As if there wasn't enough to worry about... Did you happen to meet the Riverfolk tribe? They're very much like us, only they're bad. Evil. And the reason they're evil is that their river has dried out.
It used to be different around here: we, the Lakefolk, would fish in the lake and the Riverfolk would fish in the river. Everyone was happy. There was enough food and enough space to satisfy everyone. Then the river started to dry out all of a sudden.
We always got along well with our neighbors! So when they hit hard times we let them have half our lake. Eldress Lake is big and can feed many mouths! But instead...
Our nets are getting torn, our fishing spots ransacked... And now our villagefolk are disappearing. And the Riverfolk don't even want to talk to us and won't let us into their village. My brother went to see them to try and resolve the issue in a neighborly fashion, but he never returned. And now it turns out he's been sitting in a draconid cage all this. Looks like the Riverfolk have been giving our waterfolk away to the draconids! There must be payback... I mean, their behavior is not very neighborly!
Well, did you teach those scoundrels a lesson? Even if they all turn to water, I won't shed a single tear, trust me on that!
Aha! That'll teach them how to ruin our nets and scare away the fish! Grr, blasted troglodytes! Serves them right!
Kill Snap the Riverfolk, the Riverfolk chieftain, and return to Smack the Lakefolk in the village on Eldress Lake.

I've been thinking... The Riverfolk did not attack us on their own volition. We have lived side by side for many moons! Every spawning season we got together and celebrate. When we'd catch a 350-pound catfish, we always invited them over for a feast. Our relations were friendly, like proper neighbors!
But after the old Plop the Riverfolk died, a new chieftain took over, named Snap. Ever since then there's been no peace between us.
I think that Snap is rotten. He's got a rotten heart, and that rot is spreading through the entire Riverfolk tribe. He's the one turning them against us, no one else would do it. And if you pierce his rotten heart right through, that would put an end to all this animosity between our tribes, and we'd go back to peaceful coexistence, like before. Please, help my race, will you?

We Lakefolk are a peaceful race. Those who come with good intentions are treated with respect. But aggressors get what they deserve. Eldress Lake is big and deep... And the fish don't mind a treat every once in a while.

I heard screams coming from the other shore of the lake. That must have been the end of that rotten Snap the Riverfolk. Oh, I hope they pick out a decent chieftain, so that we may live in peace like before.
And you, beanpole, have earned the respect of our tribe. Here is your due reward!
Board an astral sloop and go to the Frontier.

Excellent job, Keeper of the Revelation. I knew you'd be able to crush our enemies right in their lair!
But don't let it go to your head! We've won the battle, but not the war. It turns out that our enemies have settled on an island named the Frontier.
Judging by the scouts' reports the draconids and the wormfaces were unable to overcome their thousand-year animosity after all, and have resumed their fighting once more. I'm sure you realize that this is to our advantage.
Regretfully, there aren't that many Attendants here in the Citadel who are ready to fight. This is why we've hired mercenaries: orcs, humans, elves, gibberlings and others who stay true to the Master's Word. I hope you'll be able to cooperate with them, so that together you'll crush the vile traitors.
Now go. Board an astral sloop and be on your way. May the Master's Will protect you!
Hey, we know you! Keeper of the Revelation... Gosh, we envy you so much!

When the draconids and the wormfaces quarreled with the Master, we just happened to be here. Working on building the Outpost, yeah. This place was run by the draconids. Drakes, draconids and shamans performed their rituals. They say even the draconid queen, whom they call "mother," dwells here. Though we've never seen her... Just imagine how huge she must be, eh?
But then all hell broke loose! Bang, bang, golems here, draconids there, and massacre all around. Right. Our Outpost turned out to be right on the frontline. With draconids pushing on one side and wormfaces crawling out of subterranean tunnels on the other, we found ourselves smack between a rock and a hard place!

I fear the draconids will prove useless. If their chieftain knows nothing, the rest of them know even less. They're absolutely brainless.
We need to capture and interrogate a wormface. A draconid told me that the wormfaces are hiding underground and controlling the golems remotely. But how can we get them underground? I'm no gopher...
Wait a sec, I have an idea. A golem can't be controlled directly as it's not alive. This means the wormfaces are using some kind of a remote control device. If we capture such a device and study it, we'll find out where the signal is coming from.
Will you do it? All you need to do is break apart a few golems and bring me all the parts that at least vaguely resemble a transmitter. In the meantime I'll think about how to make a device that will help us find the wormface.
I think I understand now how to track down the wormfaces who are operating the golems. But it's still too early to talk details.
Cool, now I have a rough sketch. Now let me try something...
Use the locator to find the hiding wormface, use a thunderstone to make him come out and interrogate him.

All right, so this wire goes here... The gear goes there. Tighten the screws. Close the circuit... Let's check it... There's a signal! Hurray!
I really didn't expect it to be so easy. I must admit that wormfaces have fantastic technology. Anyway, I managed to modify the golem's receiver into a primitive locator. From now on the device will emit a shrill squealing sound in response to the control signal that comes from the wormface operating the golem. The closer the wormface, the louder the squealing will be!
All you need to do is find the spot where the squealing is especially loud. That will be the spot where the wormface is hiding underground.
Remember the thunderstones? I have some here. Oh, I also tinkered with them when I had some free time... Anyway, they're now a bit louder than normal stones... I'd say three times as loud, hehe. I don't have a lot of them, but I can spare you for your cause. If you detonate this stone above the wormface's head, he will pop out of the ground like a cork out of a bottle. Ready to repent for all sins, even those he didn't commit. I'm telling you this as an agent! Whose agent? Umm... Nobody's agent, I work for myself. Now go and don't fill your head with needless ideas. You'll be safer that way!
Light, blasted light! I've gone blind!
What on earth do you want from me?! Ask, I'll tell you all I know... Argh, cursed light! It's burning!
Relay the information obtained from the wormface to Larisa Dymkina.

Damn it! You loyal underlings of Nihaz don't understand a thing. All the lies have poisoned your minds! And this blind faith will lead you to your graves!
Long ago our race believed Nihaz. And what became of us? Worthless, pathetic creatures living underground! Argh... The cursed sun is burning my eyes!
Sarn, the mad Sarn had cast a Curse that almost killed us all. Those who survived ran to Nihaz in fear. They prayed for salvation, pleading for protection against the Curse. He laughed and turned the surviving Junes into wormfaces. Aye, we changed and the June Curse disappeared. We kept our lives... But can this be called life?! Eternal wretched existence in the dark, eternal fear, eternal anguish and boredom...
We hate Nihaz, and our hatred is centuries old. And now is our chance to exact vengeance! On a small shard east of the Frontier there's a teleport that's been preserved by sheer luck. It can let through an entire army! We'll infiltrate the Dead City, crushing everything in our path, and capture that which will grant us redemption. Let the gods continue their wars. And we'll depart for a place where no one will disturb us. This miserable world can continue its prolonged agony. We don't give a damn!
Well, have you learned anything interesting?
Inspect the terrain around the Outpost and report the recon results to Outpost commander Gammon the Tempestuous.

Enemies everywhere! Sprang up as if out of the ground... Well, at least the wormfaces did, literally. And we don't even know the tac... tas... damn it. Forgot the word!
Anyway, we need to scout the area and see who's where. What if the enemies are hiding something interesting? And we don't know it! That won't fly! We're scouts, after all, and we must know everything.
Only we can't leave this place. We need to meet up with other fighters to explain to them the tac... tas... tactical situation, there! Explain the tactical situation!
Good thing you were sent to our aid. Help us, will you? All you need is to carefully inspect the terrain around the Outpost. Our kind is few in number at the Outpost, so we have no one to send out on patrol. What if the enemies are scheming up to attack? Forewarned is forearmed. That's what mothers told us since we were babies!

You say the fuzzies sent you? What fuzzies? Oh, the Watchful Family! That's what I call them, hehe. Don't worry, I'm not one to pay a creature's skin color any mind. As long as you're a good fighter, everything else is unimportant.
The entrance to the wormface cave is to the north. That's bad, very bad. We're talking literally a stone's throw from the Outpost.
And the draconids have an altar in the ruins that's teeming with their priests? And they're keeping the slimies caged? Oh, that's a bad sign. Wherever magic is involved, it's wise to expect ill things. Better smash their heads in with your fist before they use it, hehe!
Destroy the draconids' altar in the Tuk-Miktu Ruins and report to Gammon the Tempestuous at the Outpost upon completion.

Look, I had this idea... Yeah, I can think too, imagine that! Pay no mind to my size and stupid-looking mug. If anything, that's my mom's fault. Well, I like me some grub, too, just like any other orc. But my brain still works like a well-oiled machine, believe that! Anyway, what was I talking about...
Right! It's time we tan the draconids' hides some. I'm sick and tired of them! Those scaly bastards have entrenched themselves in the ruins to the east, working their vile magics undisturbed. They built an altar and snatched up a bunch of slimies. Been guarding them like hawks, too! The little ones... I'm talking about the Watchfulls... They were on a recon mission and barely managed to save their furry butts! And that road is how we get our reinforcements. I bet my tooth it's no accident that the scaly bastards are working their sorcery there! They're scheming up something dirty and devious!
Go to the Tuk-Miktu Ruins and wreak some havoc! Smash the altar to bits, and make the draconids choke with anger! Well, how do you like that plan? Hehe.
And when you're done, go to the Outpost and report to our superior. His name's Gammon the Tempestuous. Tell him Cake is carrying out his duties perfectly, keeps alert when standing guard and all that good stuff. Your reward won't be long in coming either, hehe!
Hey, fighter, where do you come from? I haven't seen you around here before. What if you're a spy, eh?
Wow. You say Cake sent you here? And kicked some draconid butt along the way? That's the way we do it! I came, I saw, I smashed to pieces! Keep it up, soldier! I'm grateful to you, hehe!
Release the captured waterfolk in the Tuk-Miktu Ruins and report the rescue to chieftain Smack the Lakefolk.

Look... Here's the deal. We're trying to come to an agreement with the slimies that live by the lake. Like, we give them glass beads and they give us... Nope, not gold. What the hell do we need gold for?! We're running out of grub to eat, and you can't eat gold!
So, we want to make a deal with their leader. We want to trade! Exchange trinkets for grub like fish and crawfish... Only those Lakefolk are stubborn like damn trolls. They refuse to deal outright! We don't want nothing fancy either. Hunger's a real bitch, we're willing to settle for the basics but they still won't budge!
So here's what I think. The Watchfulls report that some of the captured waterfolk are being kept in the ruins. If you release them, the waterfolk leader might be willing to compromise. Well, do you think it will work?
What do you want in our village, beanpole?! Get lost! This is our water. Our soil. And the fish in the lake is all ours, too!

What? My brother's alive? Thank the gods! I was sure he'd turned to water by now...
Consider yourself the best friend of all the Lakefolk! I give you my word, and my word is stronger than ice!
Meet with saboteur Larisa Dymkina, who is hiding somewhere near the Smoldering Highland.

Listen up. There was a female hanging around here. A sharp cookie, and quick in all kinds of ways. You could see right away she's a saboteur, but doesn't seem to be from the committee. A damn fine woman, if only she weren't so small, hehe!
Anyway, I sent her out on a recon mission. Those Imperial saboteurs are trained specifically for these jobs. But for some reason I've had no reports from her in a long time. What if something's happened to her? I'm already short of people with no one to send out on a search mission. And so I'm forced to turn to freelancers like you.
The saboteur's name's Larisa Dymkina. In her last report she said she was going somewhere near the Smoldering Highland. Find her, will you? She might need help or something.
Looks like our reinforcements have arrived! What took you so long? What, you say you weren't receiving my reports?! Ugh, I wouldn't put it past that twit to wipe his ass with them!
Lure Broga, the draconid chieftain, into an ambush by Larisa Dymkina. Once Broga is exhausted from the fight, inject him with the truth serum and interrogate him thoroughly.

OK, what's done is done. One's as good as none, but two are a squad. Moreover, I have a plan. What plan? Very simple.
We still can't understand what the draconids and the wormfaces are doing here and why they're fighting each other. And if anyone can shed some light on the matter, it's surely the draconids themselves! You dig?
So, I caught a glimpse of a draconid in the ruins on the Smoldering Highland. It was either a chieftain or a shaman - I couldn't say for sure. You know them better. And that is why this job is for you.
The plan is this: we need to lure the chieftain into an ambush and interrogate him. The problem is he's almost invulnerable in his lair. I don't know how, but he always keeps a protective spell on himself, and that's something I know a lot about. But if we lure him out of the camp and into an ambush, I'll be able to dispel his magic. And then all we have to do is inject him with truth serum, and he'll start talking like nobody's business. In the committee we... Oops! I didn't say that, understand?
Here is the truth serum from my personal supplies. Don't ask me where I got it. Lure the draconid chieftain into my ambush. We'll tire him out by fighting and then you'll inject him with the serum. He'll soften up some, and that's when we'll get all the truth out of him.
Me not tells you a thing! Not tells... Not tells... Tells... Tells? Tells! Me tells all things! Your asks... Asks... Me talks...
